title: In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Extended Version)
why: The canonical statement of Raft's safety rules and their argument: election restriction by log up-to-dateness (section 5.4.1), the commit-only-current-term rule (5.4.2), the leader-completeness proof sketch (5.4.3), and two-phase joint consensus for membership changes (section 6).

title: Consensus: Bridging Theory and Practice (PhD dissertation)
version: Stanford University, August 2014; read the LaTeX sources at github.com/ongardie/dissertation commit 0c10ea1b (master HEAD, 2016-05-24) on 2026-10-11, which are what this pinned PDF was built from
why: The long-form treatment a learner needs for this part: chapter 3's safety argument, chapter 4 on membership changes (single-server changes as the primary algorithm, joint consensus in section 4.3 as the arbitrary-change alternative, plus availability issues), and Appendix B's formal safety proof with the TLA+ specification.

title: TLA+ specification for the Raft consensus algorithm
why: Best for reading the basic algorithm as a machine-checkable state machine, including the history variables used in the safety proof; note that it models the static-configuration algorithm only, not membership changes.

title: etcd-io/raft (Raft library used by etcd)
why: Best for seeing both mechanisms as production Go: the vote-time up-to-date comparison (raft.go:1220-1222 calling raftLog.isUpToDate) and joint-consensus configuration bookkeeping (confchange.Changer.EnterJoint at confchange/confchange.go:57 with tracker/quorum).

title: Planning for Change in a Formal Verification of the Raft Consensus Protocol
version: CPP 2016 (5th ACM SIGPLAN Conference on Certified Programs and Proofs), read 2026-10-11
why: Best for the machine-checked counterpart of chapter 7's proof sketch: a Coq/Verdi proof of state machine safety for Raft that had to discover and prove about 90 invariants, which shows where the informal argument is subtle and needs strengthening.

title: etcd documentation: Runtime reconfiguration
version: etcd v3.5 docs, page last modified 2021-10-26
why: Best for the operator-visible rules that follow from chapter 8: change one member at a time, add a member as a learner and promote it only after it has caught up, and the strict-reconfig-check guard against losing quorum during a change.

title: bug in single-server membership changes (raft-dev mailing list)
version: thread started 2015-07-10 by Diego Ongaro, read 2026-10-11 (also listed in the dissertation errata)
why: Best for the correction every reader of the thesis needs: a counterexample where concurrent single-server changes across a term boundary in an even-sized cluster overwrite a committed entry, the scope of the bug, and the fix that a leader may not append a configuration entry until it has committed an entry in its current term.

title: Safety of Raft single-server membership changes (Diego Ongaro gist)
why: Best for the case analysis that carries chapter 7's leader-completeness argument over to membership changes, enumerating the configuration relationships in which the overlapping voter must exist under the patched single-server rule.
